messages:
maria: Quick ask — can someone run a focused quality sweep comparing INT4 vs FP8 for the 7B LLaMA-variant on our instruction dataset? I'm seeing a ~1.8 pt drop in Rouge-L on a small sample and want a full check. Thread start 1768509999.

kai: I'll take it. Which checkpoint and quant config do you want me to use? `model:v2.3-llama7b` and two quant profiles `q/int4.yaml` and `q/fp8.yaml` sound right?

maria: yes, pin to `v2.3-llama7b`. Use `eval/instr-10k`. Report ppl, Rouge-L, exact-match (code tasks), chrF for translation-ish items, token-level divergence, and hallucination signals (if possible). Run with cache on/off. Include 95% CI if you can.

kai: running now. command I'm using:
```
./bench/run_eval.sh --model v2.3-llama7b --quant int4 --dataset eval/instr-10k --cache on --workers 8 --out /tmp/int4-sweep.json
./bench/run_eval.sh --model v2.3-llama7b --quant fp8 --dataset eval/instr-10k --cache on --workers 8 --out /tmp/fp8-sweep.json
```
ETA ~45m.

deploy-bot: Deployed bench-runner image `bench:v1.12` to bench-cluster (job: bench-1768509999).

ash: fyi i've seen similar before — int4 tends to drift on instruction-style tokens, especially when responses exceed 512 tokens. watch for repetition/hallucination.

kai: first pass done. quick numbers (median over 3 runs):
- FP8: ppl 12.1, Rouge-L 62.0, exact-match 48.3, chrF 0.71
- INT4: ppl 12.8, Rouge-L 60.2, exact-match 45.9, chrF 0.68
Token divergence @50 tokens: INT4 vs FP32 = 3.4%, FP8 vs FP32 = 1.2%
Logs/artifacts: `/tmp/int4-sweep.json`, `/tmp/fp8-sweep.json` (also pushing to s3).

oliver: thanks. Did you try `--cache off`? Caching can sometimes mask quantization regressions because repeated KV lookups hide token drift.

kai: yes — with cache off: INT4 Rouge-L 59.6, FP8 61.7. So gap widens a bit without cache.

nina: PR #4821 contains the updated quant calibrator we used for FP8 — that helped a lot on the fp8 side. Can you also run INT8 as a safety baseline? And add `chrF` to the table (good call).

maria: good points. @kai please add INT8, include per-task breakdown (code vs general instructions vs translation), and drop top-3 prompt diffs where exact-match diverged. Put outputs in s3 `s3://redwood-evals/1768509999/`.

kai: will do. Interim recommendation from this sweep: INT4 shows ~2.0–2.5 pt Rouge-L regression vs FP8 on instr-10k, and higher token divergence. Hallucination proxy (answer length growth + novelty score) up ~9% for INT4 vs FP8 on long-answer subset.

ash: +1 to holding default for now. We should also run hallucination checks on the long-answer subset and run human micro-evals on the top diffs.

maria: agreed. Please don't merge the quant-change PR to default until we have the extended hallucination checks and INT8 baseline. I'll link numbers in the PR thread.

kai: uploading artifacts, job finished 1768514200. s3://redwood-evals/1768509999/{int4-sweep.json,fp8-sweep.json,int8-sweep.json,summary.csv}, logs at `/var/log/bench/1768509999/`.

maria: thanks all. I'll open a follow-up with a small human eval sample and add a short checklist for release. Leaving merge on hold until we sanity-check hallucination cases. :eyes: 

oliver: i'll run hallucination-specific probes tomorrow morning and ping results here.

maria: <@oliver> appreciated — closing this thread for now, will reconvene once we have micro-eval + INT8 baseline.
